title: A Glasshouse for the Weather
premise: Mara Blackwood, a professional letter-writer who sends postcards to her family's burned-down house as a private ritual of grief, is hired by Edele Voss, the last fluent speaker of a dying language, to transcribe her memories before dementia erases them. As Mara records Edele's words, she uncovers a decades-old injustice: Edele's testimony against a powerful orchard family was buried, and her daughter was taken from her in retaliation. Mara must choose between the duty of transcription — recording only what she's told — and the justice of intervening, while confronting the question her own family never asked before her mother's memory dissolved: what actually happened that night. The novel ends with Mara testifying at a restitution hearing in Edele's language, phonetically learned, then mailing one last postcard to the burned house with a return address on it.
about_author: Ulyana Oyelaran is a former court stenographer who spent six years documenting testimony in small-town courthouses across the American Midwest. She now lives near Lake Michigan, where she teaches community classes in endangered-alphabet calligraphy.

chapters.title: The Smile That Ends Conversations
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. We meet her at her letter-writing stall, composing other people's apologies and love notes while she privately mails postcards to an address that no longer exists. A stranger watches her too long; the beat is guarded loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: A Student, Singular
chapters.summary: Edele Voss arrives at the stall asking for 'one final student' to record her language before it goes. Mara refuses twice, then accepts for money she tells herself she doesn't need. POV alternates between them. Beat: reluctant contract, first crack in the armor.

chapters.title: Words With No English Neighbors
chapters.summary: First sessions at Edele's glasshouse conservatory. Mara learns untranslatable words — grief-verbs, weather-nouns for emotions. Edele slips and mentions 'the girl.' Mara notices but writes nothing down. Beat: intimacy forming inside professional distance.

chapters.title: What the Orchard Owed
chapters.summary: Edele's memory fractures mid-session and she relives 1979: her testimony about the Halloran orchards' poisoned wells, the hearing that vanished from records, her daughter Lise taken 'for her own protection.' Mara researches at night. Beat: the past stops being background.

chapters.title: Postcards to Ash
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, interior chapter. She confronts why she writes to the burned house: her mother's dementia-era accusations, the fire no one explained, the question her family arranged itself around without ever asking aloud. Beat: parallel griefs aligning.

chapters.title: The Halloran Reply
chapters.summary: Mara contacts the surviving Hallorans under a false pretext; the youngest, Theo, recognizes Edele's name and warns her off with genuine fear rather than menace. Rising stakes: someone else is watching the glasshouse. Beat: danger enters quietly.

chapters.title: Lapse
chapters.summary: Edele forgets Mara entirely for three days, then remembers everything except the last decade. In the confusion she reveals where Lise went — alive, renamed, forty miles away. Mara must decide whether finding Lise betrays or honors Edele. Beat: moral pivot.

chapters.title: The Daughter Who Was Renamed
chapters.summary: Mara tracks down Lise, now a hospice nurse with no knowledge of Edele. Lise refuses contact — until Mara plays a recording of a lullaby in the dying language. Climax approaches: Lise agrees to come, but only if Mara can prove the buried testimony. Beat: hope with conditions.

chapters.title: Testimony, Recovered
chapters.summary: Climax. At a county restitution hearing Mara presents the recordings and Edele's original affidavit, found lining a drawer in the glasshouse. Edele, lucid for one final hour, gives testimony in her own language; Mara translates through tears. The Halloran estate concedes. Beat: justice outside the law finally entering it.

chapters.title: Return Address
chapters.summary: Resolution. Edele dies in early spring; Lise sits with her at the end, learning four words. Mara teaches the language's alphabet at the community hall, keeps the glasshouse running, and mails a final postcard to the burned address — signed, with a return address. Beat: grief converted into continuation.
